transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I came in today because I've been dealing with something at work that's... bothering me. I'm a secondary school teacher, and lately, I just can't shake this feeling that certain staff emails and the morning announcements are actually coded messages about me. 

Some of my colleagues have gently shown me that the emails were sent to the whole staff, and I see the distribution list, but... I still just feel like there's a specific, hidden meaning in them meant just for me. It's been hard to ignore, so I thought I should probably talk to someone about it.
Have you had similar thoughts or concerns outside of work, or is this something that only seems to happen in relation to your job?

No, I haven't really noticed it anywhere else. It... it seems to just happen at work. When I'm at home or out running errands, everything feels normal. It's really just tied to the school and the people there. Once I leave the building for the day, I don't get that same feeling that things are being directed at me.
Have you ever had any other unusual thoughts or beliefs that others might find strange or hard to understand, even if they weren't related to work?

No, I... I don't think so. I haven't really experienced anything else like that. It's just the situation at the school. Outside of those emails and the morning announcements, my thoughts and... well, my life in general, are pretty ordinary. I don't have any other beliefs that people would find strange or hard to understand. It's really just this one specific thing that's been bothering me.
Have you ever experienced any unusual perceptions, like hearing voices or seeing things that others around you don't seem to notice?

Well, yes, actually. I... I do hear something sometimes. It's not at work, though. It usually happens when it's really quiet, like when I'm alone in my house, or right after all the students have left my classroom for the day. 

I'll hear a woman's voice. She just says my name, or maybe makes a really short comment about whatever I happen to be doing at that moment. It's... it's so clear that I've actually answered out loud a few times, before I realize that there's nobody else in the room with me.
How long have you been hearing that voice, and have you ever told anyone about it before?

It's been about four months. Both the things at work—the messages in the emails and announcements—and hearing the woman's voice... they both started around the same time, about four months ago. And no, I haven't told anyone else about the voice. You're the first person I've mentioned it to.
When you hear the woman’s voice, does it seem like it’s coming from outside of you, or do you realize that it’s not actually there?

Well, I... I'm not entirely sure how to answer that. It definitely sounds like it's coming from outside of me, like a real person is standing right there in the room. That's why I end up answering out loud. 

But... once I look around and see that I'm completely alone, I realize she isn't actually there. So, in the exact moment it happens, it feels very real, but right after, I know it can't be.
When you hear the woman's voice, does it ever seem to be commenting on what you're doing or thinking in a continuous way, like a running commentary?

No, it's not like a running commentary. Like I mentioned before, it's really just... short comments. Sometimes in the quiet of my house, or right after the classroom empties out, I'll just hear her say my name, or maybe make one quick remark about what I'm doing right in that moment. It's never a continuous thing. Just those brief words that are clear enough to make me answer back before I realize no one is actually there.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that you hold onto strongly, even if others might say they don’t make sense or aren’t true?

Well, yes, actually. That's... that's a big part of why I decided to come in. I just can't shake this feeling about work. 

I keep getting this strong sense that certain staff emails, and even the morning announcements over the loudspeaker, are actually coded messages directed specifically at me. My colleagues have tried to tell me otherwise. They'll gently point out that the emails were sent to the whole staff list, or that the announcements are just standard school business. And logically, I hear what they're saying. But I just can't let go of the feeling that there's a hidden meaning in them, meant only for me.
Have you ever felt that messages or hidden meanings were directed at you outside of work, such as through public announcements, media, or other channels?

No, it's really just at work. I haven't noticed anything like that when I'm watching TV at home, or reading the news, or... or anywhere else, really. It's just those emails and the announcements at the school. Outside of that, everything seems completely normal.
Have you ever had any other situations, even outside of work, where you felt certain that things people said or did had a special or hidden meaning that was directed at you?

No, I really haven't. Like I said, it's... it's just the things at work. The emails and the morning announcements at the school. I don't get that feeling anywhere else, or from anyone else. When I'm out at the grocery store, or talking to my neighbors, or just going about my day... everything feels perfectly normal. It's really just confined to the school.

Even though your colleagues have shown you that the emails were sent to everyone and that the announcements are standard, do you still believe strongly that they are meant only for you, and is there any situation or evidence that could make you doubt that belief?

Yes, I... I do still believe it. That's really the main reason I came in to see you. I just can't shake the feeling that those staff emails and the morning announcements at the school are actually coded messages about me. 

Even when my colleagues sit down and gently show me the screen, proving that the emails were sent to everyone... I look at their proof, and I hear them, but it just doesn't change my mind. I still feel completely certain that the messages are meant for me. I don't really know what evidence could make me doubt it at this point, because the facts are right in front of me and I still can't let it go.

Even though you said the emails were clearly sent to everyone and the announcements are standard, do you feel like your belief about them being directed at you is completely certain and beyond any doubt at all?

Yes, I... I do feel completely certain. That's exactly why I'm here. I know it sounds strange, and I see what my colleagues are showing me when they pull up the email list, but... I just can't shake the feeling. I am absolutely convinced those staff emails and the morning announcements are coded messages about me. Even with the proof right there, the feeling doesn't go away. There's no doubt in my mind when I hear or read them.
Even when someone clearly demonstrates that the emails or announcements are not directed at you, do you still feel absolutely certain—without any doubt at all—that they are meant for you?

Yes. I know I keep saying the same thing, but... yes. That is exactly why I came in here to get help in the first place. 

I just... I can’t shake the feeling that those staff emails and the morning announcements at the school are really coded messages about me. Even when my colleagues gently show me the screen and prove they were sent to everyone, it doesn't change anything for me. I look right at it, but the certainty just doesn't go away. I still believe without a doubt that they're meant for me.
Even when someone clearly demonstrates that the emails or announcements are not directed at you, do you still feel absolutely certain—without any doubt at all—that they are meant for you?

Yes, I am completely certain. I know we've gone over this, and I know it sounds illogical, but that's the truth of it. 

When I read those staff emails or hear the morning announcements, I know they are coded messages about me. My colleagues will pull up the email, point to the 'To' line, and show me that it went to the entire staff directory. I see it with my own eyes. But it doesn't matter. The feeling of absolute certainty that the message is actually directed at me, specifically... it doesn't waver at all. That's why I'm sitting here talking to you.
